The second test version of **NetSketch**. It protects your work, adds a printable report and a shopping list that leaves out what you already own, and makes the phone app much quicker and sturdier for walking a whole home.

> **Beta:** 105 automated tests run on Linux, Windows and macOS. The Windows and macOS builds and the phone app haven't been tried by hand on every system yet. Please report anything odd under [Issues](https://github.com/NilsBriggen/netsketch/issues).

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `NetSketch-0.2.0-x64.msi` | **Windows 10/11**: installs NetSketch with a Start-menu entry, and `.netplan` files open in it |
| `NetSketch-0.2.0-x64-portable.exe` | Windows, without installing |
| `NetSketch-x86_64.AppImage` | **Linux** (x86-64, GTK 3): `chmod +x NetSketch-x86_64.AppImage`, then run it |
| `netsketch-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | **macOS** on Apple silicon: unpack and run `netsketch` |
| `NetSketch-Survey-0.2-beta.apk` | **Android 10+**: the companion app for measuring Wi-Fi on site. It installs over 0.1-beta. |

The builds aren't code-signed:
- **Windows:** SmartScreen may say the publisher is unknown. Choose *More info → Run anyway*.
- **macOS:** if it refuses to open the app, run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine netsketch` once.
- **Android:** allow installing apps from your browser or file manager when it asks.

## New on the desktop

**Your work is safe**
- "Recover last session" really brings back last session's plan. Before, the start-up plan replaced the recovery copy after 30 seconds.
- Closing with unsaved changes asks whether to save, and the window title shows • while something is unsaved.
- *Save as* (Ctrl+Shift+S), a new empty plan (Ctrl+N), and a list of recent plans next to *Open*.
- Undo can no longer make Ctrl+S write one plan over another plan's file.
- Only real plans open as plans: a phone survey or another JSON file can't be overwritten by mistake.
- Drop plans, phone surveys and floor-plan pictures onto the window.

**Plan and share**
- **Printable report:** *Export* now makes a web page that any browser saves as PDF. It has each storey drawn with its Wi-Fi map, the access points and their channels, the coverage, the shopping list, open problems and the address plan.
- **Shopping list:** one line per model you picked, leaving out what's already in the home. Phones, computers and TVs count as owned; tick *I already have this* on any device to change that. The demo home now costs about €1000 instead of €5000.
- **What good Wi-Fi means to you:** browsing, video calls or 4K and gaming. The coverage score, the Wi-Fi map colours and the legend (now with dBm) follow your choice.
- **Floor-plan pictures are saved inside the plan,** so a plan you send to someone keeps its floor plan. After adding a picture, NetSketch asks you to measure one wall you know, to scale it.

**Fixes**
- More of the interface is translated into German: problem texts, port names, the Wi-Fi map legend and messages.
- More edits can be undone: port changes, powerline kits, cable routes, floor-plan pictures, imported readings. Holding an arrow key is now one undo step.
- Importing the same phone points twice adds them once. Deleting a measured neighbour lets its networks be matched again.
- Damaged files can't blank the map or put things on impossible storeys.
- The storey list includes storeys that only hold pins, labels, a picture or a garden.
- Opening another plan stops the phone link.

## New in NetSketch Survey (Android)

- **Quick point:** records just your own network's signal in about 3 seconds, without a Wi-Fi scan. Android allows only 4 scans every 2 minutes, so a quick point lets you cover a whole home fast.
- **Ping test** to your router: average delay, jitter and loss.
- **Cancel** a measurement while it waits or runs. *Measure again here* replaces the old point instead of adding a second one.
- **The speed test always uses Wi-Fi,** never mobile data. Without Wi-Fi it's skipped.
- **Finds the computer again** when its address changed.
- The live signal graph has labelled dBm lines that follow your signal.
- Fixes:
  - A scan started by Android or another app can no longer finish a point twice, or with the previous spot's networks.
  - Points are never sent twice.
  - A spot where nothing was heard isn't saved.
  - A damaged save file is kept aside instead of wiped.
- **Permissions:** asked for on the first measurement, with a way to the app settings after a "Don't ask again". It also explains when only approximate location was allowed.
- **Display:**
  - Switching dark or light mode no longer loses a measurement.
  - The channel chart shows 5 GHz channels up to 177 and 6 GHz up to 233.
  - Taps on a zoomed plan work reliably.
  - Bigger touch targets, a plan that fits the screen, and German number formats.

## Known limits
- The built-in browser shows simple pages only.
- Catalog power draw, prices and launch years are partly estimates; each entry's note says which.
- macOS builds are for Apple silicon only.
- The phone app's ping test result isn't stored with the point.
